# Radar Classifier — Audit Review and Protocol Decision

**Date:** 2026-11-15  
**Project:** Junior Project / St Andrews–MathWorks radar UAV classification  
**Status:** Dataset integrity verified; independent physical-trial separation and generalization unresolved.  
**Basis:** User-provided `audit_report.md`, `summary.json`, and `manifest.csv` generated by read-only Codex audit. No training conducted.

## 1. Dataset integrity and partitions

| Audit item | Training | Evaluation |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Total referenced PNGs | 23,504 | 2,146 |
| UAV (1) | 11,752 | 917 |
| Non-UAV (0) | 11,752 | 1,229 |
| Timestamped source folders | 346 | 21 |

All 25,650 referenced PNG files were reported readable, 512×512 RGB, with no missing referenced files, duplicate paths, identical PNG byte hashes, or exact source-folder overlap across partitions. The audit was read-only; checks applied only to referenced real-data binary CSVs, not the synthetic images or unreferenced files. The manifest contains one checked image record for every CSV reference.

## 2. Findings requiring methodological caution

1. **Nearby source folders:** All 15 UAV evaluation folders (917 UAV images) have a same-class, same-frequency training-folder start timestamp within 30 seconds. This does **not** establish that the images share a flight trial or overlap in time; original trial IDs and recording durations are unavailable. It does mean **independence of the physical trials cannot be confirmed** from directory names alone.
2. **Acquisition-date/class association:** All non-UAV images in these two CSVs have February 6, 2024 timestamps; all UAV images have March 1, 2024 timestamps. Dates are not model inputs, but acquisition conditions could create class-correlated image artifacts. The current dataset cannot isolate date effects from the target class.
3. **No verified external generalization:** Cross-date or independently collected same-class validation is impossible to establish from the current binary CSVs. A high test accuracy would not by itself establish real-world UAV-versus-bird performance.
4. **Unresolved labels and evaluation role:** Non-UAV subtype composition, source trial boundaries, and whether the original authors' `eval_binary.csv` was used for checkpoint selection require further checking against their report and implementation.

## 3. Proposed experimental protocol (to approve before training)

**Primary baseline: reference-aligned, fixed configuration.** Use the original `train_binary.csv` (all 23,504 examples) and leave `eval_binary.csv` untouched (2,146 examples). Use ResNet18 with ImageNet-pretrained initialization, RGB 224×224 inputs, Adam with a learning rate of 1e-5, batch size 64, seed 3407, and 20 epochs as provisional settings derived from the St Andrews documentation. Inspect the reference code to verify normalization, exact transforms, loss, and model head before freezing settings. Select the **final epoch by a predeclared rule**, not by test accuracy. Run evaluation **only once after training/model selection is frozen**, and report metrics and experimental deviations. This is **reference-aligned, not a claimed exact reproduction** if the original study selected checkpoints differently.

**Later controlled experiment:** If tuning is necessary, use only `train_binary.csv` to create a reproducible, group-aware training/validation split. Infer candidate cross-sensor event groups using timestamps **only as a conservative heuristic**; document any ambiguity and retain manifests, group definitions, checksums, and seed. Never split images from the same inferred recording group. Do not use `eval_binary.csv` for hyperparameter tuning.

**Metrics:** accuracy, UAV precision, UAV recall, UAV F1, false-positive rate on non-UAV, confusion matrix, counts per class, and per-frequency breakdown. Clearly label the evaluation set and the limitations above. Comparisons to the St Andrews technical report must specify differences in preprocessing, model selection, hyperparameters, and dataset splits.

**Computation:** Use local environment for scripts, unit tests, and small-batch smoke tests. Prefer a cloud/university GPU for full 20-epoch training. Do not commit raw images or full datasets to Git.

## 4. Immediate action

Ask Codex to implement the predeclared reference-aligned PyTorch baseline and tests **without training**, after checking the existing documentation and reference code. Keep the evaluation file inaccessible to training-time decisions. Have Codex report the exact data transforms, optimizer, scheduler, classifier head, checkpoint policy, and outstanding differences from the report before execution.

## 5. Required records after training

Capture the Git commit ID, environment/package versions, hardware, data-root and CSV SHA-256 hashes, seed, pretrained weight identity, loss and optimizer, transforms, batch size, learning rate, epoch count, training logs, last-epoch checkpoint, final evaluation metrics, confusion matrix, performance by frequency, and identified limitations. Record the run as **Experiment R-001**.
